doors.label: Tax cap
doors.sentence: "Hold the line on property tax increases — stick to tax increases that residents and businesses can handle and find reasonable." No glide-path formula and no residential-rate cap. Named NO on the 7 May 2026 budget. The 9.34% residential figure is independently confirmed; the 35.52% cumulative figure is his campaign's own.

doors.label: Downtown order
doors.sentence: "Support enforcement of existing bylaws to address street disorder." No Public Order Team and no 6am–10pm bylaw hours. Scored on M33, not on M26/M27. The 2024 daytime-sheltering motion is an M33 fact and is not imported under this door.

doors.label: Housing
doors.sentence: "Victoria needs more homes, but housing policy has to work for the people who already live here." No unit target and no composition share.

doors.label: Written program
doors.sentence: Authorized 2026 site with three named commitments — a safer city, taxes people can afford, housing that works — each with a bullet list. Seven pages, financial agent named. No costings, no dates, no service standards, no lastmod.

cells.quote: Victoria needs more homes, but housing policy has to work for the people who already live here.
cells.why: Commits to volume in the right places, with no unit target and no composition share. The only named instrument is "Review the Official Community Plan using updated population forecasts", which is not M6's target-and-composition instrument and is not comparable to it — a review can lower supply as easily as raise it. 📋 Record: NO on Missing Middle, 26 Jan 2023, passed 6–3, named against with Coleman and Gardiner; at the table he said "I think Councillor Caradonna is quite right that this is not a silver bullet that addresses affordability." Matches the 2026 "not anything and everything" / "right places" clause — not a miss, not in n. Context, not scored separately: he opposed the new OCP over renter displacement and process, not over zero new homes.

cells.quote: Unfortunately, this data shows what many Victoria residents, businesses, and visitors already know: a relatively small number of shelters and parks where people shelter create a disproportionate number of police calls for service.
cells.why: He obtained VicPD call data by FOI and published it in Aug 2023: 19 shelter and encampment locations account for about 25% of all police calls; 9,363 shelter-and-park calls in 2022; more than 29,000 over 2020–22; Rock Bay Landing alone 3,337 over three years. The Program's M28 rests on this finding. Shown, not scored: it is a 2023 action and there is no 2026 sentence on data-targeted enforcement, so it is not in n. Discrepancy to reconcile in the Program, not on this card: M28 states "about 24% of 2022 police calls from 19 addresses"; the published report says about 25% of all police calls at 19 shelter and encampment locations, with 9,363 being the 2022 shelter-and-park subtotal. Fix the Program's wording before that figure is used in voter-facing material.

cells.quote: Support enforcement of existing bylaws to address street disorder.
cells.why: Commits to enforcing existing bylaws, which is M33's whole instrument (enforce existing rules, no new rules, no new staff). Comparable, not Same: daytime sheltering is not named in the 2026 bullet and the parks 7 AM standard is not stated. 📋 Record: he moved the 18 Jul 2024 motion directing staff to cost and resource ending illegal daytime sheltering in all parks and boulevards, passed 8–1 with Kim alone opposed — matches, not a miss, not a second mark. Not capped: this cell is a hit.

cells.what: drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure)
tax glide path (capped on the residential rate)
cells.quote: Hold the line on property tax increases — stick to tax increases that residents and businesses can handle and find reasonable.
cells.why: Commits to holding residential increases to what people can handle. Target, no instrument: no cap number, no year-path, no override rule, no ratio rule. 📋 Record: NO on the 7 May 2026 budget, one of three named opposed with Gardiner and Kim; the budget was 7.28% aggregate, 9.34% residential and 4.78% business. His stated reason is the opposite of Kim's — he opposed because the residential hike was too high. The vote is a hit, not a miss. Opposed −1.0 is the higher-tax treatment and is not applied. Not capped.

cells.what: CRD cost and the Goldstream plant
business, downtown, one mandate not a new office
cells.quote: Work with businesses to address security concerns and restore confidence in downtown.
cells.why: Commits to a downtown-business action. No vacancy target, no Team Victoria mandate, no Strategic Economic Plan, no Conference Centre numbers. Security cost-spreading is a different instrument and is carried on row 31, not scored from this sentence.

cells.what: capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees
Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5.
tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated)
cells.quote: When tenants are evicted for redevelopment, I want to ensure we give tenants proper compensation.
cells.why: Commits, and has taken the action: on 30 Jul 2026 he moved the amendment that raised long-tenancy compensation above the staff recommendation — 5 months' rent at 5–9 years scaling to 24 months' rent at 40+ years, moving expenses to $1,000–$1,500 — and it carried unanimously. That is M9's named compensation instrument, delivered in the campaign year. Comparable, not Same: the cluster's other limbs are absent — no 12-month notice rule, no documented right of return, no replacement-unit ratio, no Renters' Hub commitment, no STR licensing (M9b), no indoor-heat standard (M64). M9c is struck and is not scored. His 2026 platform sentence carries the same commitment: "long-term tenants should receive much stronger compensation, because many will be forced to look for new homes at today's much higher market rents." TRAC board service is professional background, not a source.

cells.what: childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is $0 → M13d)

cells.quote: For sure, we pay, the City of Victoria taxpayers pay close to $500,000 a year.
cells.why: Named mover of the 21 May 2026 motion directing staff to report on spray-paint retail restrictions to minors, secure or staff-access-only display, point-of-sale signage and retailer education, with exemptions, enforcement options, costs and consultation; carried, Caradonna and Dell opposed, Loughton absent. Commits to a graffiti instrument. Neither: retail restriction is a prevention lever and appears in none of M14 (48-hour removal standard), M16 (pests), M17 (sanitation hours) or M18 (murals). One sentence, this row: do not also mark Centennial Square or parks here.

cells.what: mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38)
walking and transit the City controls

cells.quote: He moved the 6 Jul 2023 motion asking staff to examine costs and funding mechanisms to enhance security in areas hit by crime and by the effects of encampments and supportive-housing sites: "It's a great burden, a great expense, and my motion was just to spread that out, so that where you've got problems, the whole city as a whole will come and help with that security a little bit." Defeated. That is M28b's instrument, authored and moved by him — but it is a 2023 action with no 2026 sentence naming cost-spreading, so it is shown, not scored, and not in n. The 2026 "work with businesses to address security concerns" sentence is already scored on row 18 and cannot carry a second mark. A separate 4 Jul 2024 compensation-study motion failed 4–5 and is context, not a second Record line.

cells.what: VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force)
cells.quote: Continue to support a visible police presence in Victoria's downtown.
cells.why: Commits to police presence. Neither: not the Esquimalt funding-formula settlement with mediation, and not a convene-and-publish regional services review. 📋 Record: named against cutting new patrol officers from four to two, motion carried 5–4 on 3 Mar 2026, with Alto, Gardiner and Coleman also opposed to the cut. Matching, not in n. Gardiner's "defunding the police" line is hers and is not copied onto him; the named vote is the fact.

cells.what: safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target
culture, sport, and the arts funding floor

cells.quote: Conduct a thorough review of city spending to identify expenditures that aren't needed or can be phased-in over time.
cells.why: Commits to a spending review. Neither: not zero-based, no rotating 3–4 service areas per cycle, no published three-part jurisdiction/outcomes/duplication test, no grants-over-$50K review, no savings target. The 7 May budget NO is scored on row 13, not here. Open source that could move this cell: his 10 Apr 2026 Times Colonist op-ed "Victoria is wrong to give $175K to curling club", listed on his own campaign news page, argues against a grant where a more accountable option existed — that is close to M65's grant test. The op-ed is behind a paywall and was not read this pass, so no upgrade was applied on unread text.

cells.what: local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging
trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness

cells.quote: He didn't object to a proper review of council compensation for future councils. However, he did object to sitting councillors voting themselves a large raise in the middle of their term, while residents were facing major tax increases.
cells.why: 2026 campaign text, Commits to the next-term-only rule, which is M79f's instrument exactly ("any change to Council remuneration takes effect only at the start of the following term"). Marked Partial+ rather than Partial because the instrument match on that limb is verbatim, and rather than Close because three of the cluster's other instruments are wholly absent — no published mandate letters, no lobbyist registry, no FOI-fee waiver. 📋 Record context: named NO on the March 2024 immediate raise of about 25%, and at the time said "I still hold firm to my view that whatever recommendation this panel comes to any increases must be held over to the next council"; council later backed away. FLAG: the first pass marked this Partial 1.0. See fragility note.

cells.what: neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans
cells.quote: Ensure there is sufficient funding for neighbourhood associations and cultural events that make living in Victoria enjoyable.
cells.why: Commits to neighbourhood-association funding. Neither: no grant-line number, no plain-language or French standard, no two-plans-per-year Local Area Plan programme. Cultural events in the same bullet are not scored on row 39. "Allow residents to have a real say in their city" is the same neighbourhood-voice claim, not a second mark. The OCP review is housing-planning context on row 1, not an LAP programme.

cells.what: community surveys, turnout and ballot access
Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic)
cells.quote: Named NO on 25 Jun 2026 on the non-binding ballot question, carried 5–4, opposed with Caradonna, Gardiner and Thompson.
cells.why: Reported reason: he held that there should be a meaningful vote — that is, a binding referendum rather than an opinion question. Shown, not scored, because the report is a paraphrase and no verbatim 2026 sentence was located. Do not recode this as Opposed. M81's own endpoint is to return to the Province and request a binding referendum, so a NO cast in favour of a binding vote is not opposition to the measure; it sits with M81's direction while rejecting the instrument M81 assumes will proceed.
